target_customer: Mobile app developers, ad networks and platform owners who pay for code similarity and SDK analysis
problem: App stores had no transparency into what code and SDKs apps contained, making quality, origin and malicious behavior hard to detect.
product_category: Mobile app binary analysis and security

founders.name: Nate Lawson
founders.background_notes: The YC page spells the name Kate Lawson; Dealroom says Nate Lawson founded it in 2011. No bio found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A binary similarity engine across iOS and Android apps at app store scale was hard, and the company called it patent pending.

defensibility.rationale: The index of app binaries and matching engine were hard to rebuild, but demand depended on a few buyers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple was interested in buying it by 2015 and acquired it in 2016, per trial emails and testimony reported by AppleInsider.

market_need_then: In October 2015 SourceDNA's analysis of the Youmi SDK led Apple to pull 256 apps, showing demand from the platform owner for this visibility.

brand_strength.rationale: Gained press for the Youmi SDK findings and SDK market share report, but no brand material found.

pivots.from: SDK and app trend business intelligence
pivots.to: developer tool to find coding problems (Searchlight)
pivots.why: VentureBeat says it moved beyond telling companies about app trends to helping developers fix apps.

outcome_analysis: SourceDNA built a binary similarity engine, published SDK market share and the Youmi SDK findings in 2015, and was bought by Apple in 2016, a deal that stayed unreported until the Epic v Apple trial. The price is unknown and the acquirer was also its main interested buyer.
notes: sourcedna.com did not resolve (blocked or dead), so the site was not viewed. Funding: one aggregator lists a 120K seed in August 2015, unverified and not recorded as a round. No dated competitor sources found, list left empty. Founder name conflict between YC page (Kate Lawson) and Dealroom (Nate Lawson). Apple deal rests on AppleInsider reporting trial testimony; exact date not given, so year only.
